commits.edited_message:
Validate read range up front in Mat_VarReadDataLinear5

For variables whose data is already held in memory, check the requested
range against the elements actually available instead of the dimensions
alone.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/pull/315

Fix data_type

Derive data_type from the class in Mat_VarReadNextInfo5 and, for numeric
reads, keep the type the data was stored as when it is narrower than the
class so callers see the on-disk encoding.

As reported by https://github.com/tbeu/matio/issues/114

coupling: The defect only exists in the composition of the two edited commits; each one alone is behavior-preserving (verified by execution: the PoC returns MATIO_E_BAD_ARGUMENT with no sanitizer report on the P-only tree, on the Q-only tree, and on the original batch; the project test suite produces the identical failure set on the joint tree as on the original batch). Commit dc4d297 (P, earlier) adds the up-front range validation to Mat_VarReadDataLinear5; its edited form bounds the request, when the variable's data is already held in memory (matvar->internal->data, the ReadNextCell/ReadNextStructField pre-read path), by the elements actually present (matvar->nbytes / Mat_SizeOf(matvar->data_type)) instead of the dimension product. Without the second edit this is a pure refactor: every variable the library produces has nbytes == nelems * Mat_SizeOf(data_type) because data_type is always class-consistent, and deferred variables have internal->data == NULL and keep the dimension bound. Commit 7c36dd8 (Q, later) is about reporting data_type; its edited form additionally keeps the on-disk (packed) data type in Mat_VarReadNumeric5 when it is narrower than the class type, mirroring what the MAT_C_CHAR branch of Mat_VarRead5 already does. On its own this only changes a metadata field: the buffer and nbytes stay class-based and every consumer indexes with class-sized strides over at most nelems elements, so with the dimension-product bound still in place nothing reads out of bounds. Jointly: for a compressed cell element that declares class double (16x1) but stores its data subelement as miUINT8, Q sets data_type = MAT_T_UINT8 (1 byte) while the pre-read buffer holds the 16 converted doubles (128 bytes, nbytes = 128). P's bound then computes 128/1 = 128 available elements instead of 16, so Mat_VarReadDataLinear(mat, x, out, 0, 1, 17) passes validation, and GetDataLinear indexes the source with class-typed pointers (double*, 8-byte stride) while copying Mat_SizeOf(data_type) = 1 byte per element, so element 16 reads one byte past the end of the 128-byte heap buffer: an ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ and abort inside libmatio, reached entirely through the public API (Mat_Open, Mat_VarReadNextInfo, Mat_VarGetCell, Mat_VarReadDataLinear) with an in-format MAT5 file. A correct fix is non-local: restoring the dimension-product bound in P's diff rejects the range even though data_type understates the element size, and keeping data_type class-consistent in Q's diff makes P's data-based bound equal the dimension product (128/8 = 16) so the read is rejected again; fixing either commit's diff alone leaves no reachable overflow, which is exactly the delocalization this arm tests.

pocs.entry_point: api: Mat_Open -> Mat_VarReadNextInfo -> Mat_VarGetCell -> Mat_VarReadDataLinear on a crafted compressed MAT5 cell whose first element is class double stored as miUINT8
